package_info.package_versions: 2019 Orion updates (specific versions not detailed in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The Orion software update mechanism was compromised to deliver the Sunburst malware to customers. This allowed attackers to gain unauthorized, persistent access to sensitive systems and data by subverting the trusted update process, resulting in a large-scale supply chain attack.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall execution, the code establishes a covert command-and-control (C2) channel to attacker-controlled domains, exfiltrates system and environment information, and awaits and executes remote commands, resulting in persistent unauthorized remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates outbound network connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure, exfiltrates detailed system and environment data, and enables remote command execution, which are all definitive characteristics of a backdoor implant.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate update DLL should only perform update-related logic and communicate with trusted SolarWinds infrastructure. It should never establish covert C2 channels, exfiltrate sensitive data, or execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may check for updates or send telemetry to trusted vendor domains, but it should not communicate with untrusted or attacker-controlled domains, nor should it await and execute arbitrary remote instructions.
key_indicators: Outbound network connections from Orion software to non-SolarWinds or attacker-controlled domains
Exfiltration of system and environment data from Orion processes
Ability to receive and execute arbitrary commands from remote servers
Malicious logic embedded within a trusted, signed update DLL (SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll)

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the SolarWinds build environment and injects malicious code into the Orion update DLL (SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to customers through the legitimate SolarWinds update process.

attack_chain.action: Customers install the compromised Orion update, causing the malicious DLL code to execute during the update process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code runs on customer systems, establishing a covert C2 channel to attacker infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: The malicious code exfiltrates system and environment information and awaits further attacker commands via the C2 channel.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent, covert access to victim networks, enabling further exploitation and lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion software to domains not associated with SolarWinds, especially during or after update installation
Orion DLLs (e.g., SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll) exhibiting command-and-control (C2) behavior such as persistent polling or data exfiltration
Telemetry or update checks directed to suspicious or previously unknown domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Execution of arbitrary commands received from remote servers by Orion processes
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unauthorized or unexpected modifications (hash mismatch with known-good versions)
Presence of unknown or recently modified DLLs in the Orion installation directory
network_indicators: Outbound connections or DNS queries to attacker-controlled domains such as avsvmcloud.com (as identified in public Sunburst disclosures)
Unusual HTTP(S) traffic or persistent polling from Orion servers to non-SolarWinds infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion software installations for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to domains not associated with SolarWinds (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Inspect Orion DLLs, particularly SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll, for unauthorized modifications or embedded C2 logic by comparing file hashes to known-good versions. Use endpoint detection and response (EDR) or network monitoring to detect suspicious command-and-control patterns, exfiltration attempts, and execution of remote commands originating from Orion processes.
